Why this is a standalone set and not a per-constant flag. The enum
-     * constant list above is regenerated by the recurring "sync provider model definitions" chore
-     * (e.g. #7088, #7315, #7582). That generator emits every model as a single-arg
-     * {@code NAME("value")} constant and has no notion of an extra capability argument, so a
-     * per-constant flag (the original #7531 shape, {@code NAME("value", false)}) is silently
-     * dropped on the next sync — which is exactly how #7582 reverted the adaptive-thinking opt-out
-     * and reopened issue #7526. Keeping the capability here, outside the generated constant list,
-     * lets syncs add/remove/reorder constants freely without clobbering it. Referencing the enum
-     * constants (rather than duplicating the string literals) means a sync that renames or removes
-     * a referenced constant breaks compilation instead of drifting silently.

Why this names the capable models rather than the models that reject them.
+     * It was the inverse — a set of adaptive-thinking ids — and that shape rotted twice:

+     * increasingly take no sampling params, so naming the capable ones makes the default the safe
+     * one: a model added by the recurring "sync provider model definitions" chore is assumed to take
+     * none until someone says otherwise, which omits a parameter rather than having the provider
+     * reject the whole request with a 400.
